inherited_methods.loss_step: bound the 2s-th edge prime by repeated Bertrand growth and then impose s=o(K) so that every unpadded odd part is b^o(K)
inherited_methods.lost_information: only a fixed positive fraction of the K base-b exponent is needed for the odd edge labels; one need not make that fraction tend to zero
inherited_methods.consequence: the published estimate reaches (N^(1-eta_K),N] only when K eta_K tends to infinity and does not enter a fixed multiplicative tail

inherited_methods.loss_step: hold the support parameter s fixed while sending K to infinity, because the goal was only arbitrary depth at fixed roughness
inherited_methods.lost_information: the exact exponent budget remains positive when s grows linearly with K at a sufficiently small constant rate
inherited_methods.consequence: RR.1 gives arbitrarily long paths in a power tail but does not quantify logarithmic support inside a constant-width tail

inherited_methods.method: hard or finitely nested lower thresholds
inherited_methods.loss_step: retain only the cutoff scale and discard every prime-valuation signature above it
inherited_methods.lost_information: whether a complete positive-density zero-signature fibre is necessarily retained by an o(N) cylinder deletion
inherited_methods.consequence: IR.1 refutes thresholds but does not state a single theorem covering threshold deletion combined with finite or sparse prime observations

inherited_methods.loss_step: instantiate one path avoiding a fixed finite prime set without coupling this avoidance to the tail-width estimate
inherited_methods.lost_information: edge primes may be chosen above a growing roughness cutoff while the padding prime remains outside the frozen controlled set
inherited_methods.consequence: the finite guard is not an all-parameter obstruction to growing valuation-cylinder rules

inherited_methods.loss_step: treat thresholds, prime valuations, adaptive largest-prime residues, graph neighborhoods, and arbitrary vertex labels as one class
inherited_methods.lost_information: these models have different distinguishing power and no common positive-density fibre
inherited_methods.consequence: a theorem stated for all such local rules would be unsupported and could approach the unresolved full transversal problem

required_new_information: A simultaneous choice s=Theta(K) for which the edge-prime size, initial padding exponent, balancing decrement, distinctness, and support minimality are all uniform in K.
An explicit fixed tail constant and an explicit roughness cutoff that also excludes every frozen controlled prime.
A positive-density estimate for the all-zero controlled-valuation fibre under a quantitative sparse-prime hypothesis.
A frozen cylinder-rule definition strong enough to combine thresholds and valuation observations but narrow enough not to cover adaptive residue-aware rounding.
A finite verifier that checks exact identities and inequalities without being used as the proof of the universal statement.

candidate_bottleneck.parameter_choice: m=floor(K/16), support size 2m+1, roughness cutoff y=b^m

candidate_bottleneck.balancing_budget: the one-vertex shore imbalance gives total exponent discrepancy below K+m and maximum distributed decrement at most 18
candidate_bottleneck.expected_tail: every padded vertex should lie in (b^K/b^19,b^K]
